title: Pilot latency synthesis and rollforward
header: Date: 2026-09-02 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Luis (Redwood Solutions), Mina (CSM); Tom, Sara, Devon, Alisha (Aurelia)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review recent latency runs across TTFT and streaming; align on kernel choice tradeoffs for Aurelia's mixed seqlen traffic; decide rollforward plan for canary and hedging policy. Action items assigned for perf matrix update and security doc ask.
next_steps: Jordan - send condensed perf matrix + cost delta spreadsheet by 2026-09-04
Priya - run 95th/99th TTFT sampling for seqLen>1024 and share logs by 2026-09-06
Devon - provide response distribution histogram from production traffic by 2026-09-05
action_items: Jordan (AE) - share perf matrix + cost delta (due 2026-09-04)
Priya (SE) - run targeted TTFT samples for long tails (due 2026-09-06)
Devon (SRE) - export seqLen histogram and spike windows (due 2026-09-05)
Mina (CSM) - create meeting invite for canary rollforward (due 2026-09-03)
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda - recap of last week's kernel runs, TTFT numbers, streaming first byte behavior, and decide canary path.
[00:00:18] Tom: yeah sounds good, uh we pulled together the production traces from last week, there was a big uptick on thursday that spiked the tail.
[00:00:30] Priya: ok can you say the spike characteristics again? was it long sequences or a lot of concurrent short ones?
[00:00:38] Tom: mostly long sequences, a small percentage of requests over 1k tokens, but they were heavy and coincided with batch job windows so queueing compounded it.
[00:00:50] Sara: and just to flag, our SLAs care about TTFT 95th < 400ms for interactive flows, 99th ideally < 800ms but we know that's tough.
[00:01:05] Jordan: right, so quick recap: last run we tested three kernel paths - tiled matmul optimized path, fused-attn fastpath, and the quantized fallback. overall median's fine but 95/99 tails varied.
[00:01:22] Priya: I have the numbers here - median response 120ms on fused-attn, 95th 360ms, 99th 940ms (long tail). Tiled path median 140ms, 95th 420ms, 99th 720ms. Quant fallback median 320ms but 99th actually dropped in some cases to 680ms because it avoided kernel contention.
[00:01:45] Devon: interesting, so the faster kernel had a longer tail. is that because of microburst contention?
[00:01:52] Priya: yeah likely, fused-attn uses more memory bandwidth and when KV cache thrashes or multiple large sequences hit, context switching creates jitter. tiled path is steadier due to chunked compute.
[00:02:07] Alisha: would a hedging policy help here? like start fused-attn, if not out in X ms, fallback to tiled or quant?
[00:02:14] Priya: exactly - we tested hedging with 80ms timeout to launch tiled path; that reduced 99th significantly to ~500ms but increased median by ~10-15ms and adds cost.
[00:02:28] Jordan: cost vs latency tradeoff is key for you. Tom, do you have a cost target or percentage over baseline you can tolerate?
[00:02:36] Tom: we can tolerate up to 25% higher inference spend for critical interactive features, but not higher for background routing.
[00:02:44] Jordan: good, that gives us room. Priya, can you walk through streaming first-byte observations?
[00:02:50] Priya: sure - streaming handshakes show that under pinned KV cache conditions, initial token emission delays to 60-90ms on fused-attn for long context runs; tiled path gave more consistent 30-50ms FB. We also saw a few malformed transcripts in the logs where session resync happened, probably because we hit an NRT limit. (note: transcription may mislabel 'NRT' could be "NFT" in auto transcript)
[00:03:17] Sara: that maps to user complaints where the UI shows a spinner for too long.
[00:03:20] Jordan: ok, so option set: 1) keep fused-attn as default, hedging to tiled at 80ms; 2) default tiled for seqLen>1024 and fused for short; 3) use quant fallback aggressively for background queries.
[00:03:36] Tom: option 2 appeals - route by seqLen threshold, because our traffic mix is skewed; most are short but that long tail kills the SLA.
[00:03:45] Devon: route by seqLen in the edge router? we can tag requests and let Redwood route, but adds a tagging step in our pipeline.
[00:03:52] Jordan: we support routing rules based on header or token hint, we can demo the quick rule engine. Priya, note for demo.
[00:03:59] Priya: noted. also did a quick check on KV cache hit rate - long sequences had lower effective KV reuse because of diverse prompts, so caching benefit was limited.
[00:04:12] Alisha: what's your recommendation for canary then?
[00:04:15] Priya: my recommendation: canary with route-by-seqlen defaulting to tiled for >1024, fused for <1024, enable hedging with a conservative 100ms threshold initially, and telemetry flags to watch FB and 99th for 24-72h.
[00:04:31] Jordan: that sounds pragmatic. can we quantify expected cost delta? Luis?
[00:04:35] Luis: using the current perf matrix, tiled default reduces tail but raises median cost by ~8%, hedged approach raises cost by ~18% overall due to extra work when hedges fire. We'll send the precise delta in the spreadsheet.
[00:04:49] Tom: 18% is within our tolerance for the interactive flow, as long as background is cheaper.
[00:04:55] Sara: background we want quant fallback, keep cost minimal.
[00:04:59] Priya: we tested quant fallback for non-critical endpoints - it preserved throughput and cost but produced slightly different logits distribution; recommend running the current eval set to ensure quality within thresholds.
[00:05:12] Alisha: can Redwood run the eval against quantized outputs or do we need to?
[00:05:17] Jordan: we can run an initial QA eval but we need your golden prompts to be representative. Tom, can you share the prompt set?
[00:05:23] Tom: yes I'll share a sanitized set, maybe 500 prompts, by Friday.
[00:05:29] Priya: perfect, we'll run quant and fusion comparisons and attach delta metrics: exact-match, Rouge-ish, and the cust metric.
[00:05:38] Devon: another question: how does this affect dedicated vs hosted? if we move to dedicated VDUs will kernel contention be reduced?
[00:05:46] Jordan: dedicated capacity gives more predictable isolation and you can reserve GPU pools; that reduces noisy neighbors and improves 99th but costs more. For now the hedging+route-by-seqlen should give you the majority of the benefit on hosted pilot.
[00:06:00] Sara: any compliance implications for us if we move to dedicated?
[00:06:03] Mina: dedicated plus private will let you bring KMS and VPC options; we have SOC2 docs and can start a compliance pack if needed.
[00:06:11] Jordan: ok circling back to canary plan: proposed timeline - Monday run smoke tests with route-by-seqlen rule, hedging 100ms, monitor 24h; if 99th improves and cost delta within 20% we expand traffic.
[00:06:24] Tom: sounds good. Priya any gotchas we haven't captured?
[00:06:28] Priya: only that we need to instrument token-level tracing for a short window to ensure hedges don't double-emit tokens; also watch streaming partials.
[00:06:36] Jordan: and capture KB: how often hedges triggered, which kernels used, latency histograms per kernel.
[00:06:41] Devon: I'll add logs extraction to the runbook.
[00:06:44] Alisha: ok next, pricing ask?
[00:06:47] Jordan: we'll include projected delta in the spreadsheet and a short note on amortized cost per session. Luis will follow up.
[00:06:54] Luis: yes I'll put two scenarios: hedged interactive path and tiled-by-seqlen default.
[00:06:59] Tom: can we get an end-to-end sample trace with token timestamps for a long sequence? that helped debug earlier.
[00:07:06] Priya: we can provide that, anonymized of course.
[00:07:09] Jordan: ok let's recap action items - Jordan send perf spreadsheet; Priya run TTFT 95/99 samples; Tom share prompts and Devon share seqLen histograms; Mina schedule canary meeting.
[00:07:23] Alisha: thanks everyone.
[00:07:25] Jordan: thanks team, we'll follow up in threads.
